digest.component_or_area: Cloud adapter (Jira) — rate-limit resilience and config validation
propositions: Cloud transport mutations lack per-member 429-sweep enumeration; mutations traverse four distinct 429 behaviors (direct REST no-retry, subprocess backoff-retry, dispatch-wrapper retry, non-retrying apply-phases) across two levels, each requiring layer-specific assertions at its own boundary rather than uniform attempt-count assertions.

Cloud has no config-validation tier (non-HTTPS rejection, missing-credential loud-fail, insecure-override warning) unlike DC; whether Cloud silently falls back to anonymous access or fails loudly is unestablished.

Cloud probe hardcodes resolved-status set (frozenset of Resolved/Done/Cancelled) while DC threads it from settings; the open question is whether Cloud deployments using non-standard resolved-status workflow names need a runtime config hook or whether the per-deployment constant suffices.

DC user-search method bootstrap degrades silently on DC (no _USER_SEARCH_METHODS aliases exposed) to string-match, but this degradation is untested and an accidental Cloud-side rename would look identical.

Every mutating Cloud transport member must be enumerated explicitly and classified on two axes (transport seam: ACLI subprocess / pooled direct REST / bare urlopen; dispatch level: retrying wrapper / non-retrying apply-phases / no wrapper) with duplicate-write assessments recorded for members reaching known deliberate retries.

Per-member 429 behavior must be asserted at its correct boundary (pooled REST and bare urlopen at urllib.request.urlopen for exactly one attempt; subprocess at _run_acli for bounded Retry-After backoff; dispatch-wrapped through _call_with_retry for bounded retry; non-retrying apply-phases for one attempt), and each assertion must be mutation-checked with a concrete perturbation to prove test sensitivity.
